changes.title: Endurance braking system
changes.text_new: "Endurance braking system" means a supplementary braking system able to stabilize vehicle speed over a long downhill section, with little or no wear to the conventional friction-based braking system.
changes.justification: New definition added to cover endurance braking requirements introduced in this revision.

changes.title: Functions of braking systems
changes.text_new: The braking system of every vehicle shall fulfil the following functions: (a) service braking, enabling the movement of the vehicle to be controlled and the vehicle to be brought to a halt safely, quickly and effectively; (b) secondary braking, enabling the vehicle to be brought to a halt in the event of failure of the service braking system, though at a reduced efficiency; (c) parking braking, enabling the vehicle to be held stationary on an upward or downward gradient, in the absence of the driver, the active parts being then held in the locked position by a purely mechanical device; (d) endurance braking, where fitted, enabling the vehicle speed to be stabilized on a long downhill section.
changes.text_old: The braking system of every vehicle shall fulfil the following functions: (a) service braking, enabling the movement of the vehicle to be controlled and the vehicle to be brought to a halt safely, quickly and effectively; (b) secondary braking, enabling the vehicle to be brought to a halt in the event of failure of the service braking system, though at a reduced efficiency; (c) parking braking, enabling the vehicle to be held stationary on an upward or downward gradient, in the absence of the driver, the active parts being then held in the locked position by a purely mechanical device.
changes.justification: Added function (d) for endurance braking systems to align with new definition in paragraph 2.5 and updated Annex 4 requirements.

changes.title: Braking surfaces
changes.text_new: The braking systems prescribed in paragraph 5.1 shall be so designed that they act on braking surfaces permanently connected to the wheels through components of adequate strength. Where braking effort on an axle is provided by the engine or an electric motor, a disconnect device shall be permitted provided it is driver-operable and cannot be accidentally activated.
changes.text_old: The braking systems prescribed in paragraph 5.1 shall be so designed that they act on braking surfaces permanently connected to the wheels through components of adequate strength.
changes.justification: Updated to accommodate regenerative braking in electric/hybrid vehicles. Added provision for engine/motor braking disconnect.
